Quoted: 'If there aren't enough available NAT tuples, the dropped_sent_packets_count reason is OUT_OF_RESOURCES'; a five-tuple 'cannot be reused within the TCP TIME_WAIT timeout', so many connections to one destination exhaust tuples; fixes: 'adjust the minimum number of ports per VM', dynamic port allocation (doubles a VM's allocation when it is close to running out), 'Manually add more IP addresses'. brief.situation: You are the network engineer at Fennick Outdoor. The checkout service runs on GKE nodes with no external IPs; it calls the payment provider's single API endpoint through Cloud NAT nat-east (one manually assigned IP, static allocation, 64 ports per VM). In this afternoon's load test about 4% of payment calls timed out. The flash sale starts at 18:00 with twice the load.
handover: Security policy: GKE nodes must not have external IP addresses.
The payment provider allowlists our egress IPs; adding one takes them 10 minutes after a ticket.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the GKE nodes, Cloud NAT's IPs and ports, and the single payment endpoint they all call.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

effects.finding: Each VM gets only 64 ports, and every checkout pod on a node calls the same destination: 64 tuples per node to one IP and port, reused only after TIME_WAIT.

perpod.label: How many connections does a node open to the payment API at peak?
perpod.why: Wait for the running command to finish.

neteng@cloudshell:~$ kubectl top ... ; ss -tan dst <provider-ip> | wc -l (on one node, load test peak)
410 connections (12 pods x about 34)

effects.finding: A node needs hundreds of tuples to one destination at test load, and more at sale load.

budget.label: Port budget for 24 nodes
budget.why: Wait for the running command to finish.

effects.output:
neteng@cloudshell:~$ 1 IP x 64,512 ports = 64,512 tuples available
24 nodes x 2,048 ports (sale peak) = 49,152 needed -> 1 IP is close; 3 IPs leave headroom

effects.finding: Raising ports per VM needs more NAT IPs to stay within the budget as the node pool scales.

dpa.label: Ask the provider to allowlist two new NAT IPs, then enable dynamic port allocation (min 1,024, max 8,192) with three IPs on nat-east
dpa.available: not busy and (not fixed and not harmed)
dpa.why: Already done, or the system is down.

effects.output:
neteng@cloudshell:~$ (provider ticket PAY-55190: allowlist 34.23.10.2, 34.23.10.3; confirmed 17:27)
neteng@cloudshell:~$ gcloud compute routers nats update nat-east --router cr-east --region us-east1 --nat-external-ip-pool nat-ip-1,nat-ip-2,nat-ip-3 --enable-dynamic-port-allocation --min-ports-per-vm 1024 --max-ports-per-vm 8192
Updated [nat-east].

effects.log: Each node starts with 1,024 ports and can grow to 8,192 when it needs more; three IPs give the pool room to do that. The provider allowlisted the new IPs first, so no call leaves from an address it would refuse.

alert.label: Alert on OUT_OF_RESOURCES drops and on NAT port usage above 80%, and add the port budget to the capacity plan
alert.available: not busy and (not planned and not harmed)

neteng@cloudshell:~$ gcloud alpha monitoring policies create --policy-from-file=nat-east-drops.yaml   (OUT_OF_RESOURCES > 0 for 1 min)
(capacity plan: NAT tuples per destination per node at 2x peak; review before each sale)

effects.log: Exhaustion is seen when it starts, not in customer complaints, and the next scale-up checks the port budget.

extip.label: Attach external IPs to the GKE nodes so they skip NAT

effects.output:

(nodes recreated with external IPs)

effects.log: Every node is now reachable from the internet against policy, and the provider has not allowlisted 24 new addresses: payments fail outright.

udp.label: Raise Cloud NAT's UDP idle timeout from 30 to 120 seconds
udp.available: not busy and (not harmed and not tried)

effects.output:

Updated [nat-east].

effects.log: The payment calls are TCP: a UDP timeout changes nothing about the exhausted TCP tuples.

writeup.question: For the record: why payment calls timed out, what you changed and in what order, and how it is watched.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: dropped_sent_packets_count showed OUT_OF_RESOURCES. nat-east gave each node 64 ports with one IP, and each node opened hundreds of connections to the single payment endpoint, so tuples ran out.

parts.label: Order
parts.modelAnswer: The provider allowlisted two new NAT IPs first; then dynamic port allocation (1,024 to 8,192 per VM) with three IPs. External IPs on nodes would have broken policy and the allowlist.

parts.label: Watched
parts.modelAnswer: An alert fires on any OUT_OF_RESOURCES drop, and the capacity plan budgets NAT tuples per destination before each sale.

exposedNodes.headline: Give NAT more tuples, not the nodes public IPs
exposedNodes.body: The fix for port exhaustion is more ports per VM (dynamic allocation) and enough NAT IPs, allowlisted with the provider first.

saleTimeouts.headline: OUT_OF_RESOURCES means tuples
saleTimeouts.body: Many connections to one destination share one IP and port on the far side, so each node needs enough source ports. Raise the allocation and add IPs.

ported.headline: Good: sized NAT for one busy destination

scoring.modelReasoning: The NAT drops are OUT_OF_RESOURCES: each node gets 64 ports and opens hundreds of connections to one payment endpoint. Get the provider to allowlist new NAT IPs first, then enable dynamic port allocation with a higher minimum and maximum across three IPs, and test at sale load. External IPs on the nodes break policy and the allowlist; a UDP timeout does nothing for TCP. Alert on drops and budget ports in capacity planning.
